blocks.content: Quiz: What happens if SpeedBlip ran speed tests on the main JavaScript thread instead of a Web Worker?
Tap an option below to answer:
The speed test results would be less accurate because the main thread is slower
Thread choice does not affect measurement accuracy. The Cloudflare API response times are what matter for accuracy. The issue with main thread execution is UI blocking, not measurement quality.
Thread choice does not affect measurement accuracy. The Cloudflare API response times are what matter for accuracy. The issue with main thread execution is UI blocking, not measurement quality.
TypeScript would prevent HTTP requests from running on the main thread in strict mode
TypeScript has no restriction on HTTP requests from the main thread. Fetch works anywhere. The Web Worker is an architectural choice for UI responsiveness.
TypeScript has no restriction on HTTP requests from the main thread. Fetch works anywhere. The Web Worker is an architectural choice for UI responsiveness.
The UI would freeze or stutter during each speed test because the main thread handles both code execution and DOM rendering

Correct. JavaScript's main thread handles UI rendering, event handling, and code execution. A blocking HTTP request for a speed test would prevent any UI updates until it completes - causing visible freezing.

Correct. JavaScript's main thread handles UI rendering, event handling, and code execution. A blocking HTTP request for a speed test would prevent any UI updates until it completes - causing visible freezing.
Netlify would block the speed test requests as a cross-origin security measure
Netlify has no control over which thread a browser executes JavaScript on. Cross-origin restrictions relate to the destination server, not the execution thread.
